### Loading Dataset


```{r}
library(igraph)
library(igraphdata)
library(Matrix)
library(dplyr)

# Margin helpers
def_marg <- c(5.1, 4.1, 4.1, 2.1)
no_marg  <- c(0, 0, 0, 0)

pa_road_edges <- read.table(
  "roadNet-PA.txt",
  comment.char = "#",
  col.names = c("from", "to")
)

pa_road_network <- graph_from_data_frame(pa_road_edges, directed=FALSE)

# Removes duplicate edges / self-loops
simple_pa_road <- simplify(pa_road_network)
summary(simple_pa_road)
```

```{r}
# Check for self-loops
sum(which_loop(simple_pa_road))

# Check for multiple edges between the same two nodes
sum(which_multiple(simple_pa_road))
```

```{r}
# Basic Summary Statistics

mean(degree(simple_pa_road)) # Average # of connections

summary(degree(simple_pa_road)) # Degree Distribution

vcount(simple_pa_road) # Number of Vertices (nodes)
ecount(simple_pa_road) # Number of Edges (connections)
```


```{r}
# Looking at Graph Attributes

graph_attr_names(simple_pa_road) # Whole network attributes
vertex_attr_names(simple_pa_road) # Vertex Attributes
edge_attr_names(simple_pa_road) # Edge Attributes
```

```{r}
# 1. Start with a node in a well-connected area to ensure we get a "chunk"
# Using a specific node ID that is likely to have neighbors
start_node <- V(simple_pa_road)[100] 

# 2. Get the neighborhood (nodes within 3 steps of the start_node)
# This creates a subgraph that actually looks like a road network
nodes_neighborhood <- ego(simple_pa_road, order = 10, nodes = start_node)[[1]]

# 3. Create the induced subgraph based on this neighborhood
connected_subgraph <- induced.subgraph(simple_pa_road, nodes_neighborhood)

plot(connected_subgraph, 
     layout = layout_with_fr,
     # === vertex properties 
     vertex.color = "hotpink",
     vertex.frame.color = "black",
     vertex.shape = "square",
     vertex.size = 5,
     # === vertex label properties
     vertex.label = NA,
     # vertex.label.cex = 0.3,
     # vertex.label.font = 2,
     # vertex.label.color = "red",
     # vertex.label.family = "Times",
     # vertex.label.distance = 3,
     # === edge properties
     edge.color = "red",
     edge.lty = 1,
     edge.width = 0.5,
     # edge.label = ...,
     # edge.label.family = ...,
     # edge.label.font = ...,
     # edge.label.cex = ...,
     # edge.curvature = ...,
     edge.arrow.size = 0.2,
)
```

```{r}
# colors()
red_colors <- colors()[grep("red", colors())]
orange_colors <- colors()[grep("orange", colors())]
yellow_colors <- colors()[grep("yellow", colors())]
green_colors <- colors()[grep("green", colors())]
blue_colors <- colors()[grep("blue", colors())]
purple_colors <- colors()[grep("purple", colors())]
brown_colors <- colors()[grep(c("brown"), colors())]
pink_colors <- colors()[grep("pink", colors())]
white_colors <- colors()[grep("white", colors())]
black_colors <- colors()[grep("black", colors())]
light_colors <- colors()[grep("light", colors())]



color_plot <- function(my_colors) {
  # 2. Set up a blank plot area
  plot(NULL, xlim=c(0, 4), ylim=c(0, 5), xlab="", ylab="", xaxt="n", yaxt="n")

  # 3. Loop through and draw rectangles
  for(i in 1:length(red_colors)) {
    # Calculate position
    x_pos <- (i-1) %% 4
    y_pos <- 4 - floor((i-1) / 4)
  
    # Draw rectangle
    rect(x_pos, y_pos, x_pos+0.9, y_pos+0.8, col=my_colors[i], border="black")
  
    # Add label
    text(x_pos+0.45, y_pos+0.4, labels=my_colors[i], cex=0.7, col="black")
  }
}

color_plot(red_colors)
color_plot(orange_colors)
color_plot(yellow_colors)
color_plot(green_colors)
color_plot(blue_colors)
color_plot(purple_colors)
color_plot(brown_colors)
color_plot(pink_colors)
color_plot(white_colors)
color_plot(black_colors)
color_plot(light_colors)
```
